name: @projexlight/sdk-approval
summary: Configurable approval routing for ProjexCloud: declare a Route once (trigger predicate → ordered approver steps → SLA per step) and any SDK can call requestApproval() to spin up a Request that walks the route. Approvers decide → step closes → next step opens or request closes. SLA breaches page the configured escalation persona. Used by tenant-admin destructive actions, FinServ payment 4-eyes, healthcare PHI-export sign-off, and PRD-management sign-off chains.

endpoints.description: Register an approval route (trigger predicate + ordered steps + SLA per step + escalation persona).
Open an approval request against a route. Body carries the action + evidence.
Approver decides a step (approve / reject + comment). Auto-advances or closes the request.
Read a request + every step + every decision (for the requester + auditors).

events.name: approval.request.opened.v1
events.description: Request opened; first step now pending its assigned approver.

events.name: approval.step.decided.v1
events.description: Approver made a decision; carries outcome + comment + decided_by_persona_id.

events.name: approval.request.approved.v1
events.description: Final step approved; downstream consumer SDK may proceed with the original action.

events.name: approval.request.rejected.v1
events.description: Any step rejected; the original action is blocked.

events.name: approval.sla.breached.v1
events.description: Step's SLA elapsed without a decision; escalation persona paged.

models.description: Route definition: trigger predicate, ordered approver-spec list, per-step SLA minutes, escalation persona.
Open request: tenant_id, route_id, requester_persona, action payload, status (pending / approved / rejected / cancelled).
One row per route step per request: assigned approver, opened_at, decision_at, outcome, comment, sla_due_at.

hooks.name: registerRoute
hooks.description: Service entry to declare a new route (idempotent on name + tenant_id).

hooks.name: requestApproval
hooks.description: Open a request against a matching route. Returns request_id immediately; caller polls or subscribes.

hooks.name: decide
hooks.description: Approver hook used by the gateway endpoint; can be invoked programmatically for automated reviewers (CI gates, policy bots).

hooks.name: startSlaWatcher
hooks.description: Background worker that fires approval.sla.breached.v1 when due_at slips. Safe to leave running in dev.

scenarios.title: Finance team registers a 4-eyes route for outbound payments over $10k
scenarios.when_to_use: Tenant admin sets up policy once; every Stripe payout > $10k auto-routes through finance + a senior approver before settle.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Route persisted. Emits approval.route.registered.v1. Future sdk-payment.charge calls matching the predicate spawn an approval.request automatically.

scenarios.title: Approver decides a pending step
scenarios.when_to_use: Approver picks an item from the Approvals queue in tenant-admin and clicks Approve / Reject.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Step transitions to decided; emits approval.step.decided.v1. If last step: request transitions to approved + emits approval.request.approved.v1. Otherwise the next step opens for its assigned approver.

scenarios.title: Step SLA breached → escalation persona paged
scenarios.when_to_use: Background worker spots a step whose due_at has slipped; escalates rather than letting the request rot.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Emits approval.sla.breached.v1. The route's escalation persona receives a notification (via sdk-notification); the step is re-assigned to them so they can either approve directly or chase the original approver.

scenarios.title: Automated policy bot acts as one of the approvers
scenarios.when_to_use: A CI gate or compliance bot can call decide() programmatically — useful for SOX SOD checks where the bot verifies that the requester and approver are different personas.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Bot's decision counts as a full step decision. Audit chain shows actor.kind='service' so reviewers can distinguish automated approvals from human ones.

scenarios.title: Tenant admin gates destructive operations behind approval
scenarios.when_to_use: Any 'delete all records' or 'rotate BYOK key' action in tenant-admin should route through approval rather than execute immediately.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Action is blocked until the route's steps clear. On approve: dispatcher fires the original action. On reject: UI shows the rejection comment to the requester. Either way the audit chain has the full trail.

compliance_posture.notes: Segregation-of-duties (SOX): requester ≠ approver enforced at decide(). 4-eyes (PCI-DSS Req-7): require ≥2 steps with distinct approver roles. Audit chain entries are immutable — once decided, a step's outcome cannot be edited (write a compensating action instead).

pricing_skus.unit_description: per request opened (free below plan ceiling)
per SLA-breach event (proxy for ops cost)
